methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting community access in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, embodying peer-driven distribution that could counteract metro concentration if sustained and scaled.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional depth in Richmond's metro core, but without explicit rural extension mechanisms, risks reinforcing capital-region concentration rather than statewide distribution.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Editorial explicitly naming AI data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide signals concentration of infrastructure without corresponding capability distribution—economic activity accumulates in NoVA while rural regions face externalities without benefits.

signals.title: UMW Launches Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - University of Mary Washington
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI-in-Business master's program at UMW develops deep specialized talent, but degree-based credentialing typically serves already-educated populations, deepening capability in accessible metro corridors rather than distributing skills broadly.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard deploying an AI IT assistant represents platform-delivered productivity gains requiring minimal AI fluency from users—broad but shallow adoption that increases efficiency without building deep local capability.
